result.summary: This pull request implements BIP-348 (OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK) within Tapscript, restricted strictly to regtest activation via version bits. It introduces the opcode to the script interpreter, provides verification for 64-byte Schnorr signatures against arbitrary stack messages, and adds functional and unit test coverage.
result.problem: Bitcoin Tapscript currently lacks an opcode to verify signatures over arbitrary data on the execution stack, which prevents testing and prototyping covenants and protocols such as LN-Symmetry (Eltoo). Developers and researchers need a working implementation on regtest to experiment with these designs without activating new consensus rules on mainnet.

result.card: Implements BIP-348 OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK for Tapscript on regtest only, enabling script validation of arbitrary message signatures on the stack. This provides the foundation for covenant designs and layer-2 protocols such as LN-Symmetry without modifying mainnet consensus rules. It is strategically important as part of the broader covenant design and activation debate. Review is currently stale because the PR needs a rebase and the author has been silent since May 2025. It has received several Concept ACKs and code review approval from Jeremy Rubin with no blocking technical objections.
